title: A step can act on what an earlier step was told

expect.why: The resolver is the one thing four drivers implement separately, so it gets a scenario of its own. A driver whose resolver silently matched nothing would send the literal ${...} as a session id and get a refusal here, rather than failing somewhere in the hijack flow where the cause would be much harder to see.
The id came out of an array by index. Resolving through a list is the case a resolver is most likely to get wrong, because objects-by-key is the obvious half.
The second reference reads a plain object key, and reads it out of a step that was itself reached by reference — so a resolver that only worked against the first step would fail here.
